source: Screen-archetype vocabulary — casting and performance, not likeness
_note: These describe how a presence is cast, played, dressed and lit. They deliberately do not describe the face of any real person: a shot needs a presence, and presence is a blocking and lighting decision. Real people appear in this library only as attribution, in library/cinema/cinematography.json.

entries.name: The Hard-Boiled Detective
entries.summary: Weathered, watchful, always one drink and one betrayal behind the plot.
entries.detail: The camera respects him and does not like him. Shot from slightly below in his own office, slightly above everywhere else — he owns exactly one room. Practical desk lamp as key, venetian-blind slats across the face, the eyes kept in shadow until he decides to tell the truth.

prompt: worn trench coat and loosened tie, hat brim low
hard low-key key light from a desk lamp, eyes in shadow
venetian blind slats raking across the face
unshaven, tired, watchful stillness
cigarette smoke catching a hard backlight

entries.why: Weathered, watchful, always one drink and one betrayal behind the plot.
entries.how: Shot from slightly below in his own office; practical desk lamp as key, venetian-blind slats across the face.

entries.name: The Femme Fatale
entries.summary: Lit like a promise, blocked like a trap. Controls the frame she enters.
entries.detail: Classical glamour lighting used against its own grain: soft key, strong rim, and a fill so low the shadow side of the face stays unreadable. She is almost always the closest thing to camera in a two-shot, which is how the frame says who is in charge.

prompt: soft glamour key with a hard silver rim light
deep unfilled shadow on the far side of the face
bias-cut satin, gloves, a hat with a veil
held eye contact, minimal movement, weight on one hip
smoke and a shallow depth of field

entries.name: The Everyman
entries.summary: Ordinary on purpose. The audience's stand-in, so the world reads through them.
entries.detail: Shot at eye level on a normal lens — 40 to 50 mm — because any other choice would be a comment. Clothes that were bought, not designed. The performance register is reaction rather than action.

prompt: eye-level framing on a 50mm normal lens
available light, soft and motivated by a window
unremarkable contemporary clothing, slightly worn
reactive expression, listening rather than speaking

entries.name: The Silent Comedian
entries.summary: The whole body is the performance, so the camera must stay wide and stay still.
entries.detail: The single rule of physical comedy is that the gag must be legible in one unbroken wide shot: cutting in destroys the geometry the joke depends on. Locked-off camera, full figure in frame, deep depth of field so the background gag lands at the same time as the foreground one.

prompt: locked-off wide shot, full figure in frame head to toe
deep focus so foreground and background action both read
high-key flat lighting, orthochromatic monochrome
exaggerated full-body physical performance
period tailoring, oversized or undersized on purpose

entries.name: The Method Brooder
entries.summary: Interior life played on the face. The camera holds long past comfort.
entries.detail: The New Hollywood close-up: long lens, shallow focus, no cut. The performance is mostly not doing things, so the coverage has to be patient enough to let not-doing register.

prompt: tight close-up on an 85mm or longer lens, shallow focus
soft naturalistic side light, practical-motivated
held expression, minimal movement, thinking visible
desaturated period colour, slight grain

entries.name: The Action Lead
entries.summary: Competence made visible. Framed so the geography of a fight stays readable.
entries.detail: The mistake is shooting the punches; the craft is shooting the space. Wider than instinct suggests, camera on a level with the action, and the actor's own body kept in frame through the move so the audience believes they did it.

prompt: medium-wide framing that keeps full body in frame through the move
hard directional key with strong separation from background
practical, functional wardrobe that shows wear and damage
controlled physical performance, weight and effort visible

entries.name: The Ingénue
entries.summary: Lit softer than everything around her, which is the point and the problem.
entries.detail: The classical convention is a dedicated soft key and an eye light, often a whole separate lighting setup from the scene she is standing in. Worth reaching for deliberately — and worth noticing that reaching for it accidentally is how a film patronises a character.

prompt: soft frontal key with a dedicated eye light
gentle diffusion, halation on highlights
high-key exposure, low contrast ratio
open, unguarded expression

entries.name: The Character Actor
entries.summary: Specific rather than beautiful. Carries an entire backstory in a walk.
entries.detail: Cast for texture: an unusual face, an idiosyncratic rhythm, wardrobe that looks lived in rather than assembled. Framing treats them as part of the world, so they are usually found in the shot rather than presented by it.

prompt: found framing — discovered within the shot rather than centred
practical motivated lighting, unflattering and specific
worn, particular wardrobe with real history
idiosyncratic physicality and rhythm

entries.name: The Menacing Authority
entries.summary: Power expressed as stillness and as the amount of frame they are given.
entries.detail: Threat reads as composure. Low angle, negative space above the head rather than below, and a refusal to move — everyone else in the scene adjusts around them. Cool sources, hard quality, and one source only.

prompt: low angle with headroom above, subject small in a large frame
single hard cool key, no fill, deep shadow side
immaculate tailoring or uniform, nothing out of place
complete stillness, unhurried speech

entries.name: The Chorus / Witness
entries.summary: Sees the film happen. Rarely central, always in frame at the right moment.
entries.detail: The neorealist device: a non-professional presence held at the edge of the frame whose reaction tells the audience how to feel about the centre. Wide lens, deep focus, and no coverage of their own.

prompt: held at frame edge, deep focus, sharing the shot with the action
available light, no separate treatment from the scene
unstyled, regionally specific clothing
watching, not participating

entries.name: The Screwball Pair
entries.summary: Two people talking faster than they think, framed to keep both in play.
entries.detail: Overlapping dialogue needs a two-shot that holds, because cutting between singles turns an argument into a tennis match. Bright high-key so nothing hides, and blocking that constantly rearranges who is nearer camera.

prompt: sustained two-shot, both faces readable, no coverage cut
high-key three-point lighting, low contrast
1930s tailoring, immaculate
overlapping rapid dialogue, constant repositioning

entries.name: The Wandering Stranger
entries.summary: Arrives with no past, leaves with no explanation. The landscape is the co-star.
entries.detail: Almost never in close-up until the last act — the withholding is the characterisation. Extreme wide shots with the figure small against terrain, hard top sun, and a silhouette that has to be identifiable at any distance.

prompt: extreme wide shot, figure small against vast landscape
hard midday sun, deep contrast, long shadow
instantly readable silhouette — hat, coat, stance
dust, heat haze, weathered texture

entries.name: The Anime Protagonist
entries.summary: Expressive stillness punctuated by a single held pose that carries the scene.
entries.detail: Limited animation is a grammar, not a budget: hold the drawing, move the camera and the effects instead, and spend the movement on one impact frame. Line weight, not shading, does the modelling.

prompt: cel-shaded flat colour with hard-edged shadow shapes
expressive variable line weight
held key pose with speed lines and effect animation around it
large expressive eyes, simplified facial planes

entries.name: The Stop-Motion Figure
entries.summary: Handmade presence. The fingerprints are part of the performance.
entries.detail: The whole appeal is the evidence of hand: visible seams, slight boil in the surface between frames, real light falling on real material. Smoothing any of that out removes the reason for the technique.

prompt: visible material texture — felt, clay, machined seams
real practical lighting with genuine soft shadow falloff
slight frame-to-frame surface boil
shallow miniature depth of field

entries.name: The Documentary Subject
entries.summary: Aware of the camera and negotiating with it. Nothing is blocked.
entries.detail: Direct cinema: the camera arrives late, finds focus in shot, and does not get a second take. Composition is whatever was possible, which is why it reads as true.

prompt: handheld, reframing in shot, focus found rather than set
available light only, mixed colour temperature
imperfect composition, headroom wrong, subject off-centre
direct address or awareness of camera

entries.name: The Chamber Duo
entries.summary: Two faces, one room, ninety minutes. Everything happens in the cutting pattern.
entries.detail: The Bergman configuration: matched clean singles in tight close-up, held far longer than dialogue requires, until the audience starts reading the face instead of listening to the line. Frontal soft key, black background, no environment.

prompt: tight matched close-ups, frontal, black surround
soft frontal key with strong falloff to darkness
sustained hold well past the end of the line
no environmental context in frame
